'''Otoyo no Mikoto''' (乎止与命) was a [[Kofun period]] [[Kuni no miyatsuko|local chieftain]] and one of the [[Owari clan|Owari Kokuzō]].

== Overview ==
In the ''[[:en:Kokuzō Hongi|Kokuzō Hongi]]'', he is referred to as '''Kotoyo no Mikoto''', while in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'', he is recorded as '''Koto no Mikoto'''<ref>"Kawachi Province, Kami-betsu, Tenson, Owari no Muraji" in the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', Kōnin 6 (815).</ref>.

The ''Kokuzō Hongi'' states that he was appointed as the [[Owari clan|Kokuzō of Owari Province]] during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ar|الإمبراطور سيمو|arz|الامبراطور سيمو|azb|سیمو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Seimu|cs|Seimu|de|Seimu|es|Seimu Tennō|fa|امپراتور سیمو|fi|Seimu|fr|Seimu|hr|Seimu|hu|Szeimu japán császár|id|Kaisar Seimu|it|Seimu|ja|成務天皇|ka|სეიმუ|ko|세이무 천황|nl|Seimu|pl|Seimu|pt|Seimu|ru|Император Сэйму|sh|Car Seimu|simple|Emperor Seimu|sl|Cesar Sejmu|sv|Seimu|th|จักรพรรดิเซมุ|tl|Emperador Seimu|tr|Seimu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Сейму|uz|Imperator Seimu|vi|Thiên hoàng Seimu|yo|Emperor Seimu|zh|成務天皇|zh_min_nan|Seimu Thian-hông|zh_yue|成務天皇|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}}.

His son, [[Takeinadane]], succeeded him as the Owari Kokuzō, and his daughter, [[Miyazu-hime]], became the wife of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}. The {{ill|Hikami Anego Shrine|ja|氷上姉子神社|qid=Q11549548}} in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}} enshrines [[Miyazu-hime]], with a tradition linking it to the residence of Otoyo no Mikoto.
